prerequisites: Signed arithmetic, fractions, ratios, powers, linear equations, and coordinate graphs
learning_outcomes: Track the types and charges entering a simple interaction
Check a small allowed contraction and a forbidden alternative
Explain the role of the supplied doublet and vacuum coordinate
Derive a scaffolded charge-preservation and algebraic mass relation
Separate matrix structure from its numerical coefficients
Track energy changes without inferring a transition rate

requested_deliverables: capstone.md with full answers and rubric
assumptions: A topical short course, not a semester per topic. Pacing is 55-minute core lessons plus capstone periods; split dense lessons if actual learner load requires it.
No prior calculus, abstract algebra, university linear algebra, or quantum mechanics unless explicitly taught earlier.
Required core assessments must be solvable with taught finite examples. Clearly label deeper recognition-only extensions.
Markdown is the delivery format; no PDF or Word generation is required.

course_map.assessment_target: Track the types and charges entering a simple interaction

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Carry the course15 typed sectors forward. Specify H_phi in W of bidegree(0,1),q=3,Y=1/2 and its Hermitian-dual covector barH with q=-3. Read each of the four source interface formulas before computing its charge.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Up inputs u^c(2,0),Q(1,1),H(0,1) have q=-4+1+3=0 and total bidegree(3,2). Neutrino inputs nu^c(0,0),L(3,1),H(0,1) have0-3+3=0 and(3,2).

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Down inputs d^c(2,2),Q(1,1),barH covector: charges2+1-3=0; contracting one weak slot first leaves d^c at(2,1), then top degree(3,2). Electron e^c(0,2),L(3,1),barH gives6-3-3=0, contraction yields e^c at(0,1), then(3,2).

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Replacing barH by H in down gives2+1+3=6 and is not the same interface. Zero charge alone cannot replace the declared color/weak contractions or the top-form check.

course_map.title: Invariant contractions
course_map.worked_example_capability: Check a small allowed contraction and a forbidden alternative
course_map.assessment_target: Check a small allowed contraction and a forbidden alternative

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Teach iota_l(v1 wedge...wedge vk)=sum_j(-1)^(j-1)l(vj) times the remaining wedge. Use ordered basis c1,c2,c3,w1,w2 and Omega their full wedge. Omega^-1 extracts the top-form coefficient. Explain covariance: transform every vector by U and the covector by l U^-1; detU=1 preserves Omega.

worked_example.task_and_answer: iota_w1*(w1 wedge w2)=w2 and iota_w2*(w1 wedge w2)=-w1. For up use u=c1c2,Q=c3w1,H=w2: product=+Omega. For nu use nu=1,L=c1c2c3w1,H=w2: +Omega.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For down use d=c1c2w1w2,Q=c3w1,barH=w1*: contraction givesc1c2w2 and Q wedge that is+Omega. For electron e=w1w2,L=c1c2c3w1,barH=w1*: contractionw2 yields+Omega. Using H=w1 with L endingw1 gives zero because a basis factor repeats; this is a zero component, not a new allowed nonzero scalar.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: An arbitrary charge-zero product need not be top degree. Check signs, vector/covector type, weak slot removed and final degree(3,2). Under diag(i,-i,1,1,1), the color phases multiply1 and the tested scalars remain unchanged; under a weak phase the covector must transform inversely.

supplemental_exercises.explanation: Apply a block-unitary diagonal action to all vector and dual slots. Covectors acquire inverse phases. Verify the evaluated scalar directly before the general covariance statement.
supplemental_exercises.worked_task_and_answer: Take weak diag(i,-i) and identity color. For upQ containingw1 gainsi,H=w2 gains-i, so product factor1. For neutrinoL endingw1 gainsi andH=w2 gains-i, again1.
supplemental_exercises.practice_task_and_answer: For down,d=c1c2w1w2 has weak phase1,Q=c3w1 gainsi,barH=w1* gains-i, so final factor1. Electron e=w1w2 has1,L endingw1 gainsi,barH gains-i, again1. Separately choose upu=c1c3,Q=c2w1,H=w2: one color swap gives-Omega; nuL=c1c2c3w2,H=w1 gives-Omega. Thus signs may differ while invariant scalar character remains.
supplemental_exercises.diagnostic_task_and_answer: If barH is incorrectly transformed as a vector with phasei, the down/electron product acquiresi*i=-1; this falsifies that mistyped action. Retain the failed sign and repair the dual rule.

course_map.title: The Higgs doublet interface
course_map.worked_example_capability: Explain the role of the supplied doublet and vacuum coordinate
course_map.assessment_target: Explain the role of the supplied doublet and vacuum coordinate

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Teach the two Higgs components explicitly: H=(H_plus,H_zero), T3=diag(1/2,-1/2),Y=I/2 and Qelectric=T3+Y. Treat v as a supplied nonnegative magnitude with declared mass units in the compiler convention; no numerical vacuum scale is derived here.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Qelectric=diag(1,0), so upper charge+1 and lower charge0. Supplied vacuum(0,v/sqrt2) is annihilated by Qelectric. At synthetic v=2 mass units, vacuum=(0,sqrt2), norm squared2.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: At synthetic v=4, vacuum=(0,2sqrt2), norm squared8 and Qelectric times vacuum=(0,0). A test vector(1,0) has Qelectric output(1,0), so placing a vacuum solely there does not preserve this generator.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A charge-neutral lower component states which generator leaves that vector fixed; it does not choose v, potential coefficients, vacuum stability or transition rate.

course_map.title: Unbroken charge and mass formulas
course_map.worked_example_capability: Derive a scaffolded charge-preservation and algebraic mass relation
course_map.assessment_target: Derive a scaffolded charge-preservation and algebraic mass relation

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Use the supplied compiler quadratic-form formulas mW^2=g2^2 v^2/4 and mZ^2=(g2^2+gY^2)v^2/4. Define cos²theta=g2²/(g2²+gY²), then cancel factors to derive rho=mW²/(mZ² cos²theta)=1 where the denominator is nonzero.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Synthetic dimensionless g2=3,gY=4 and v=2 mass units gives mW²=9,mZ²=25,cos²theta=9/25,rho=1. These are algebraic outputs, not measured masses.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Synthetic g2=4,gY=3,v=2 gives mW²=16,mZ²=25,cos²theta=16/25,rho=1. Doubling v doubles the positive masses and multiplies squared masses by4; couplings and ratio stay fixed.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: At v=0 both squared masses vanish but the displayed ratio is0/0; do not claim it is numerically evaluated there. Matching scale and couplings remain recorded inputs. Deriving these substitutions does not derive the physical quadratic form from an untaught field theory.

course_map.title: Yukawa maps and mixing inputs
course_map.worked_example_capability: Separate matrix structure from its numerical coefficients
course_map.assessment_target: Separate matrix structure from its numerical coefficients

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Treat Yukawa coefficients as a supplied matrix mapping a specified finite family input to output. Separate carrier-compatible structure from numerical entries, mixing basis and normalization. Use2x2 synthetic action and explicitly retain input/state records.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Synthetic Y=[[1,2],[0,3]] acting onf=(2,-1) gives(0,-3). Same allowed matrix shape with different entries can give different outputs. In a declared classroom mass convention M=(v/sqrt2)Y, v=sqrt2 makes M=Y.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Synthetic Y=[[2,0],[1,1]],f=(1,2) gives(2,3). Relabel both input/output by swap P: Yprime=P Y P^T=[[1,1],[0,2]], fprime=(2,1), outputprime=(3,2)=P(2,3). Retain Y and P; structure alone does not select them.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Do not infer mixing angles or Yukawa values from charge cancellation. A basis change must transform vectors and matrices together; a source state-coordinate list is not a table of measured coefficients.

course_map.worked_example_capability: Track energy changes without inferring a transition rate
course_map.assessment_target: Track energy changes without inferring a transition rate

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Keep a typed action/energy ledger. Read the six source action sectors as architecture with supplied coefficients and boundary states; assess only finite additive energy differences and signed residual reconstruction, not an untaught variational derivation.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Synthetic energy ledger in common units: before(5,2,1),after(4,4,1) gives signed components(-1,+2,0), totals8->9,net+1. If a model predicts+.8, retained residual+.2 restores actual+1. No rate follows without a time/update model.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Before(3,1,2),after(2,1,1) gives(-1,0,-1),totals6->4,net-2. Prediction-1.5 plus residual-.5 restores-2. Retain labels, signs, endpoints and any supplied external transfer; an unclosed balance remains a named residual.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Source S_native,S_gauge,S_fermion,S_Higgs,S_Yukawa,S_TG label action terms, not automatically separately measured energies. An energy difference has no time dimension and cannot determine a transition rate by itself.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For the worked ledger record synthetic g2=3,gY=4,v=2, chosenY and basis, finite contraction examples, mass identities and energy residual. Potential coefficients and matching scale are unspecified inputs; do not fill them from symmetry alone.

Mark masses/mixing measurements as possible constraints, rate data as additional transition information, and scale/state assumptions as required metadata; no observation is invented.
